agent_notes: All 150 IDs got a definite answer on the first try, with no retries needed: 60 returned HTTP 401 (hidden products) and 90 returned CRAWL_NOT_FOUND. None returned HTTP 200, so no IDs in this chunk are published products. All 90 not-found IDs also returned CRAWL_NOT_FOUND on /wp/v2/media, so none are attachments. They are other post types or were permanently deleted. The hidden products fall in 71-157, a range mostly of hidden products that also contains 75-77, 114, 133-134, 152-153 and 158-159, which are not products.

Chunk 2 (IDs 413-562). All 150 IDs returned CRAWL_NOT_FOUND (404) on /wp/v2/product/{id}, and again on /wp/v2/media/{id}. They are either other post types (such as pages, posts, variations, orders or revisions) or were permanently deleted. Because every result was a 404, it is worth running a control fetch on a known published product ID. That would rule out Exa returning NOT_FOUND for these REST URLs in general.

Chunk 3 (IDs 563-712): all 150 IDs returned CRAWL_NOT_FOUND on /wp/v2/product/{id} and also CRAWL_NOT_FOUND on /wp/v2/media/{id}. There were no 200, 401/403 or transient errors, so no retries were needed. This means the whole range is neither a product nor a public or hidden attachment. These IDs are either permanently deleted, belong to other post types (posts, pages, revisions, variations, orders, nav items), or are unused auto-increment gaps. Uniform 404s across a whole range could also mean Exa is getting 404s for another reason, so check this against a chunk known to contain published products.
